claims.text: The proposed intervention is a controlled in-situ laser remelting/annealing pass after deposition of each layer.
Standard additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components exhibit residual stress.
Standard additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components exhibit columnar grain structures.
Standard additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components exhibit interlayer porosity.
The laser remelting pass induces partial remelting and controlled resolidification of the just-deposited layer.
In-situ laser remelting reduces thermal gradients during fabrication.
In-situ laser remelting reduces residual stress.
In-situ laser remelting refines the grain structure.
In-situ laser remelting diminishes porosity at layer interfaces.
A refined, more homogeneous microstructure with lower residual stress and porosity improves dimensional accuracy.
A refined, more homogeneous microstructure with lower residual stress and porosity improves mechanical properties.
Relative to standard fabrication without remelting, the intervention will reduce warpage.
Relative to standard fabrication without remelting, the intervention will enhance tensile strength.
Relative to standard fabrication without remelting, the intervention will reduce brittleness.
Relative to standard fabrication without remelting, the intervention will produce fewer microscopy- and nondestructive-testing-detectable defects.
The intervention is expected to be most effective for laser-powder-bed-fused high-entropy alloys in moderate-to-complex geometries.
The efficacy of the intervention may vary across alloy systems and additive-manufacturing techniques.
